hints: Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane: normal reaction $R = mg\cos 25^\circ$.
As the particle slides down, friction acts up the plane with magnitude $F = \mu R = 0.4mg\cos 25^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law down the plane: $mg\sin 25^\circ - 0.4mg\cos 25^\circ = ma$.
Cancel mass $m$ from every term: $a = g(\sin 25^\circ - 0.4\cos 25^\circ)$ and evaluate with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$R - mg\cos 25^\circ = 0 \implies R = mg\cos 25^\circ$$

Since the particle is sliding, the friction force has reached its maximum value:
$$F = \mu R = 0.4 \times mg\cos 25^\circ = 0.4mg\cos 25^\circ$$

Set up Newton's second law down the incline:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies mg\sin 25^\circ - F = ma$$
$$mg\sin 25^\circ - 0.4mg\cos 25^\circ = ma$$

Cancel the common factor of $m$ across all terms:
$$a = g\sin 25^\circ - 0.4g\cos 25^\circ$$

Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and compute the values:
$$10\sin 25^\circ \approx 10 \times 0.422618 = 4.22618$$
$$4\cos 25^\circ \approx 4 \times 0.906308 = 3.62523$$
$$a = 4.22618 - 3.62523 = 0.60095\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Round to 3 significant figures:
$$a = 0.601\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: The particle starts from rest, so initial velocity $u = 0$.
Use the constant-acceleration formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $t = 3\text{ s}$ and acceleration $a = 0.601\text{ m s}^{-2}$ from part (i).
walkthrough:
State the SUVAT formula connecting distance, initial velocity, uniform acceleration, and time:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$

Substitute the given parameters: $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (released from rest), $t = 3\text{ s}$, and $a \approx 0.60095\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$s = 0 \times 3 + \frac{1}{2} \times 0.60095 \times 3^2$$
$$s = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.60095 \times 9$$

Perform the calculation:
$$s = 4.5 \times 0.60095 = 2.704275\text{ m} = 2.70\text{ m} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
